analysis.investment_thesis: CIE Automotive India is a well-run but mediocre auto components business — nearly debt-free with solid FCF, but delivering sub-threshold ROCE of 14.7% and ROE of 11.8% while trading at a demanding 22.5x P/E that assumes a quality moat which isn't there. At this price, you're paying a premium for a cyclical, commoditized business in a sector facing structural EV disruption.
key_strengths: Aggressive deleveraging: borrowings collapsed from INR 1,648 Cr (2020) to 426 Cr (2025), D/E now 0.06 — near debt-free balance sheet
Strong FCF quality: FCF/Net Income of 107% (INR 885 Cr FCF vs 828 Cr net profit in FY25), OCF positive all 5 years
Operating leverage evident: operating income CAGR of 11% outpacing revenue CAGR of 6.5% over 9 years
key_risks: EV disruption: core products (crankshafts, CV joints, transmission parts) are ICE-heavy — structural demand risk as India's EV adoption accelerates
Mediocre returns: ROCE 14.7% and ROE 11.8% are below Munger's 15%+ minimum threshold; not a compounder at these economics
Revenue cyclicality: revenue swung from 8,032 Cr (2018) down to 6,050 Cr (2020) and net profit turned negative in 2022 — confirms deep cyclicality with OEM volume dependence
red_flags: Highly volatile 'Other Income': swung from -749 Cr (2022) to +409 Cr (2023) — this is almost certainly goodwill impairment/write-offs, making reported net profit unreliable; 2022 net loss of -136 Cr was largely driven by this line
Valuation mismatch: 22.5x P/E and 19.85x EV/EBITDA for a business with 11.8% ROE and 6.5% 9-year revenue CAGR is pricing in excellence that isn't present in the numbers
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Applying inversion first: what makes this a bad investment? A cyclical auto components supplier with ROCE of 14.7% — barely above the cost of capital for such a business — selling at 22.5x earnings. The operating margin of 8.19% is thin, leaving little buffer against volume declines (as 2020 showed with operating profit halving to 502 Cr). The "Other Income" volatility is deeply concerning: -749 Cr in FY22 (likely impairment on the Mahindra CIE restructuring when Mahindra exited) followed by +409 Cr in FY23 (reversal/disposal gains). This makes the reported 19.3% net profit CAGR misleading — underlying operating earnings compound at a far more modest pace. Management has done an excellent job eliminating debt, but that's a one-time tailwind now largely exhausted.

The business is structurally exposed to EV transition risk — crankshafts, CV joints, turbocharger housings, and transmission components are ICE-specific or heavily ICE-weighted. Unlike bearing or brake companies that carry over to EVs, CIE's product mix skews toward powertrain components under threat. At 19.85x EV/EBITDA with EBITDA margins of ~15% and tepid revenue growth, the stock is priced for a quality moat that doesn't exist. A fair price for this business would be 12-14x EV/EBITDA — implying 25-35% downside. I'd want to see ROCE sustain above 18%, revenue accelerating to 10%+ CAGR, and a credible EV pivot before revisiting. As Munger says: a fair business at a fair price is still just a fair business.
